# WO-2026-08-09-07 — Archive the best-value judgement

## Warwick has changed his mind, and this is a REMOVAL order

His words, and they are the specification:

> *"I have changed my mind on the 'best value' rule. **ARCHIVE IT.** Do not make Terra, the planner,
> or the browser phase attempt to optimise Ariel/other choices by live price, price-per-wash,
> multibuy maths, or bargain judgement before handing the list to the browser. … The objective is
> deliberately to SIMPLIFY the handoff … Do not push bargain-shopping complexity into that path. …
> For now, Warwick remains the bargain hunter at the ASDA end. … **AsdAIr should prepare the right
> shop reliably. It does not need to become a supermarket arbitrage desk.**"*

**This order REMOVES capability. That is the point.** Resist every instinct to preserve the clever
part. A smaller, simpler rulebook path is the deliverable, not a regression.

## What is archived, and Larry's one judgement call

- **Rule 31** — *"Ariel Pods: pick the BEST VALUE by price-per-wash"* — **archived**, named by Warwick.
- **Rule 36** — *"if a multibuy gives ≥50% off the EXTRA item(s), buy up to the offer quantity"* —
  **archived**, it is multibuy maths, which he named.
- **Rule 37** — Sure pair rounding, *"any 2 for £X: round qty UP … "* — **Larry's call: archived
  too.** It is multibuy-conditional and cannot be evaluated without offer evidence at plan time,
  which is precisely what Warwick removed. **Recorded as Larry's reading, not Warwick's words.** If
  you think that reading is wrong, say so in your return — do not act on your disagreement.

**What the rulebook is STILL for, and must keep doing:** carrying genuinely non-price household prose
— rotation, out-of-stock meaning, exclusions, aliases — to the reasoning consumer. **The prohibition
on growing a deterministic mini-language is unchanged and unaffected.**

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — The price/bargain judgement is gone from the rulebook path.** No price-per-wash, no
  multibuy arithmetic, no cheapest/best-value comparison anywhere `applyRulebook` can reach. Remove
  it; do not leave it behind a flag. **A dormant code path is the thing Warwick is trying not to
  have.**
- **AC2 — R1's AC3 tests are RE-CUT, not deleted.** Their three cases were exactly rules 31, 36 and
  37. The rulebook's remaining job is real, so replace them with cases proving a genuinely non-price
  household rule changes a line with attribution. **If your final test count is lower than 29 in
  `rulebook.test.js`, justify every removed assertion by name in your return.** A silently shrinking
  suite is how removed capability becomes removed coverage.
- **AC3 — A CONTROL that fails if price arithmetic re-enters.** Written so it can be made to fail:
  mutation-test it by reintroducing a price comparison and showing it goes RED, then restore. **Pin
  it to something outside the module under test where you reasonably can** — that is this estate's
  established shape for a prohibition control, and `rulebook.test.js`'s existing AC6 test is the
  worked example to follow.
  ⚠️ **If you scan source text, split on `/\r?\n/`, never `'\n'`.** The estate's files are CRLF and
  that exact defect false-positived a control on this branch today.
- **AC4 — `runPipeline.js` stops claiming a determinism it does not have.** The comment at `:1441`
  asserts *"planBasket is pure and deterministic, so given the same durable inputs it reproduces the
  same plan"*. **That is false** — the rulebook consults the model at every recomputation (measured:
  3 consults on a full journey). Make the comment true about **current** behaviour. **Do NOT change
  behaviour to make the old comment true** — the remembered-last-choice work is a separate order and
  yours must not anticipate it.
- **AC5 — Counts, all eight suites, before and after.** Assert the count, never the exit code. Any
  decrease must be explained line by line. **`skill` must still show exactly its 7 pre-existing
  environment failures and no eighth.**
- **AC6 — Nothing is resurrected to compensate.** Warwick: *"do not resurrect CDP price-shopping or
  Terra/browser back-and-forth to compensate for removing the value rule. Continue through the
  existing accepted browser contract."* Assert in your return, against your own diff, that you added
  no browser round-trip, no new Terra call, and no price fetch.

## Required evidence

- All eight suites executed with **counts** before and after: `pipeline`, `handoff`, `packet`,
  `browser-runner`, `bot`, `intake`, `reconcile`, `skill`. Verify my baselines in
  `capability_evidence` rather than trusting them.
- The AC3 mutation output, **both directions**, pasted, with a byte-identical restore check.
  **Mutate a copy or restore in a `finally`.**
- `node services/asdair/handoff/mutation-proof.js` → must still report `9/9 guards proven
  load-bearing`.
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/asdair/skill/rulebook.js services/asdair/skill/rulebook.test.js services/asdair/skill/README.md services/asdair/pipeline/runPipeline.js` → report exit code AND coverage. Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED, never a pass
- **The archival SQL, WRITTEN BUT NOT EXECUTED.** Give me the exact statement that would archive
  rules 31, 36 and 37 in `asdair.rules`, with the current `status`/`directive` values it expects.
  **You hold `live_authority: none` and `credential_scope: none` — do not connect to any database.**
  The rules are Warwick's data and the live change is mine to run under his authority.

- The `packetLinesFromPlan` attribution gap and `decisionSpine.test.js:78`'s CRLF defect — both

5. Write your return to `Deliverables/2026-08-09-return-B15-R3-archive-best-value.md` — **this path

**You are the only writer in `C:/Fusion247PKA-b153-int`.** If you observe a commit you did not make,

**The ceiling, unchanged:** no real shop has run. B15-3 is not live-complete until the integrated
